tests: baseline: clean order, should ask nothing
say: Hi, can I get two cheeseburgers and a cola.
Can I get two, uh, actually three chicken sandwiches and a lemonade.

tests: swapping an item in a later turn
say: A hamburger and onion rings, please.
Actually, make the hamburger a veggie burger.

tests: fixing a quantity in a later turn
say: Sorry, I meant two iced teas, not four.

tests: a correction that could mean either item; the agent should ask which
say: A cheeseburger and a chocolate shake.
Fries, onion rings, and a side salad.

tests: taking back one modifier and keeping another
say: A cheeseburger with no pickles and no onions.
Oh wait, I do want pickles. Just no onions.

tests: fillers and a wrong word replaced mid-sentence
say: Um, can I get a, uh, vanilla, no, strawberry shake and, uh, a water.

tests: a cut-off word and several modifiers in one breath
say: I'll have a chick-, a chicken sandwich with extra cheese and add bacon, and a large fries.

tests: an item not on the menu, then replacing it
say: Can I get a pepperoni pizza?
(if asked, or next) Never mind the pizza. Just a hamburger and a cola.

tests: correcting a size you said wrong
say: One small lemonade and a veggie burger with no tomato.
Wait, I said small? I want a large lemonade.

tests: a longer order with several separate changes
say: Can I get three hamburgers, two fries, and three colas.
Add an iced tea, no ice.
